title: Changing Y to I & Dropping Silent E Rules
objectives: Apply consonant + y -> i rule before suffixes
Drop silent e before vowel suffixes

teacherNotes.content: Present the pronunciation/reading rule for: Changing Y to I & Dropping Silent E Rules. Use the 14 Gabarit fields to clarify rule, system, logic, and exceptions.

teacherNotes.title: Anticipated Problems & Solutions (CELTA Standard)
teacherNotes.content:
⚠️ Problem: Learner writes *studiing with double i.
💡 Solution: Highlight rule: Y never changes to I before -ing!

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Changing Y to I & Dropping Silent E Rules
1. Definition: Core suffix addition rules governing letter changes at root boundaries.

2. Rule: 1. Consonant + y -> change y to i before any suffix except -ing (happy -> happily, study -> studied BUT studying). 2. Drop silent e before vowel suffix (-ing, -ed, -er), keep before consonant suffix (-ful, -less) (hope -> hoping, hopeful).
3. Why? Prevents double 'ii' spellings and clarifies vowel length.
4. How to recognize? Observe root ending in y or silent e before adding suffix.
5. Common examples: happy -> happily, beauty -> beautiful, reply -> replied, hope -> hoping / hopeful, care -> caring / careful
6. Counter-examples: Vowel + y = keep y (toy -> toys, play -> played).
7. Exceptions: dyeing (preserving e to avoid dying), argument (arguing drops e), truly (true drops e).
8. Common mistakes: Writing *studing instead of studying or *hopeing instead of hoping.
9. Mnemonic / Hint: Consonant + Y becomes I! Drop E for Vowel suffix, Keep E for Consonant suffix!
10. Key vocabulary: y-to-i rule, silent-e dropping, vowel suffix, consonant suffix, root boundary
11. Frequency: ★★★★★ (Essential)
12. CEFR Level: 🟡 A2
13. Associated Visual: 🔄 Y transforming into I; Silent E dropping into bin before vowel suffix.
14. Key Takeaway: Consonant+Y -> I! Drop E before vowel suffix!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: Why does 'happy' become 'happily' but 'play' becomes 'played'? (happy has consonant+y -> i; play has vowel+y -> keep y)
CCQ 2: Why do we keep 'y' in 'studying'? (To avoid double 'ii')
CCQ 3: Do we drop silent 'e' in 'hopeful'? (No, -ful starts with a consonant)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.

elements.content: Combine root and suffix correctly:
🎯 Item: happy + ness = ? ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: happiness
🎯 Item: care + ing = ? ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: caring
🎯 Item: care + ful = ? ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: careful
